groups.instructions: The passage has six paragraphs, A–F. Which paragraph contains the following information? You may use any letter more than once.

questions.prompt: an explanation of the origin of a word
questions.explanation: 'The word "placebo" comes from Latin and means "I shall please".'

questions.prompt: a biological explanation of how a placebo can reduce pain
a reason why some improvements may be wrongly attributed to placebos
questions.explanation: Natural cycles and 'regression to the mean' 'can easily be mistaken for a placebo response'.

questions.prompt: an example showing the influence of a practitioner's manner
a description of how new medicines are tested
questions.explanation: The controlled trial procedure is described step by step.

groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

questions.prompt: Placebos have been shown to shrink tumours.
questions.explanation: Paragraph C: the effect is 'largely confined to symptoms that patients report themselves … rather than to measurable conditions such as tumour size'.

questions.prompt: Blocking endorphins weakens the placebo effect on pain.
questions.explanation: Paragraph D: 'the placebo effect is significantly reduced'.

questions.prompt: The nocebo effect is more common in older patients.
Pills in plain packaging tend to have a weaker placebo effect than branded ones.
questions.explanation: Paragraph E: 'branded tablets outperform those in plain packaging' — the same idea expressed the other way round.
questions.trap: Paraphrase reversal: 'A outperforms B' = 'B is weaker than A'.

groups.instructions: Answer the questions below. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage for each answer.

questions.prompt: In which year did Henry Beecher publish his paper?
What fraction of patients did Beecher say responded to placebos?
questions.explanation: Paragraph B: 'around a third of patients'.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do illnesses such as colds follow, which explains some improvement without treatment?
questions.explanation: Paragraph C: 'illnesses follow natural cycles'. Note that 'regression to the mean' (four words) would break the three-word limit — always count.

questions.prompt: What name is given to placebos that patients know are inactive?
questions.explanation: Paragraph F: 'these "open-label" results'. Hyphenated words count as one word.
